original_metadata.title: The normalized first and second Fourier transforms on quantum Euclidean space are mutual inverses on the specified polynomial-Gaussian union spaces for zero less than q less than one
original_metadata.author: Kevin Coulembier
original_metadata.source_title: The Fourier Transform on Quantum Euclidean Space
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: Ordinary Fourier inversion does not apply to braided coordinates with two inequivalent q-differential calculi. The author derives the spherical Fourier kernel by a graded Laplacian induction, reduces each harmonic block to paired q-Hankel transforms, and evaluates their action on q-Laguerre weighted bases with exact Jackson-integral normalization. These computations prove that the two explicitly constructed transforms are inverse on the specified Gaussian union spaces.

proof_review.note: Read both exact Fourier Definitions3/4 and Theorem7, the complete spherical-kernel induction Theorem6 and Lemma7, the q-Laguerre generating-function/orthogonality calculations(3.1)-(3.2), monomial expansion and inverse q-Hankel Theorem3, and Gaussian integration/context Sections2-4. Published Fischer decomposition and standard q-Laguerre orthogonality are explicit prior background; all new inverse-normalization and Bochner core is authored in the pinned source. V_[alpha] and barred V_[beta] are algebraic unions of the precisely shifted polynomial-Gaussian spaces, not an arbitrary L2 space. The Hilbert-space oscillator extension and separate derivative identities are excluded from counting. Original selected statement/core pages rendered and visually inspected; exact header and native ZIP members verified. Editorial scope and warnings are retained.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem7 for quantum Euclidean dimension m at least3, 0<q<1 and alpha,beta>0. The first transform of Definition3 from barred V_[beta] to V_[1/beta] and the second transform of Definition4 from V_[alpha] to barred V_[1/alpha], with their exact author normalizations and opposite signs, compose to the identity on these algebraic polynomial-Gaussian union spaces. No arbitrary analytic function space or Hilbert extension is claimed.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The source uses overbars to distinguish two transforms and Gaussian spaces; unchanged native TeX and original pages retain these bars that text extraction may lose. General-function q-Hankel statements elsewhere require all terms to be well-defined; the selected claim uses only the explicitly specified polynomial-Gaussian spaces.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The full original Theorem7 is bundled with both exact Fourier definitions, algebraic Gaussian union spaces, quantum coordinate/calculus and Fischer foundations, q-Laguerre generating/orthogonality formulas, monomial inverse-Hankel calculation, Gaussian integration, full spherical-kernel induction and Bochner relations. The transforms use opposite signs and the exact authored Jackson normalization. Published Fischer decomposition and standard q-Laguerre orthogonality remain cited background. No Hilbert-space extension or separately counted transform helper is selected.
